page: Google Cloud Platform z3-highmem-22-highlssd is a memory-optimized and storage-intensive server instance. It features 22 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 11 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 176.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is a key feature, consisting of three NVMe SSDs totaling 9663 GB of bundled local storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark results place this instance in the average performance tier for most compute and memory tasks, with some strong highlights. It achieved a PassMark CPU score of 28161.46 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11804.0. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1494.87 GB/sec and a large block uncached write speed of 45.38 GB/sec. In database operations, the server processed 24.07 million Redis SET operations per second and scored 10342.95 in PassMark database operations. Notably, it demonstrated strong performance in LLM text generation using a small 135M model, reaching 298.77 tokens per second, while prompt processing for a medium 7B model registered at 112.16 tokens per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the z3-highmem-22-highlssd offers high resource density by combining a substantial memory footprint with massive, high-speed local NVMe storage on dedicated Intel Xeon hardware. This eliminates the need for external storage attachments for high-throughput workloads, though the lack of complimentary public IPv4 addresses should be factored into networking designs. The server is highly suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale caching layers, data warehousing, and local file processing tasks that require low-latency access to large datasets.
